name: arc-expand-markers-in-color-panels
description: Use when an ARC grid has large solid color-3 panels containing color-2 markers. Replace each marker's 3×3 neighborhood within the panel with color 1, preserving the marker and all outside cells.
---

# Expand markers within colored panels

When a grid contains one or more rectangular regions of color 3, with scattered color-2 cells both inside and outside those regions:

1. Identify the contiguous rectangular color-3 panels/regions.
2. For each color-2 marker located inside a panel, recolor its centered 3×3 neighborhood to color 1.
3. Preserve the color-2 marker itself. Do not modify zeros or other colors outside the 3×3 influence, and do not expand color-2 markers outside the color-3 panels.
4. Overlapping neighborhoods simply combine; keep every original marker as 2.
5. Preserve the input grid dimensions and all unaffected cells.

A useful check: a marker near a panel boundary can paint cells just beyond the original panel edge, as long as they are within its 3×3 neighborhood; zero cells outside the influence remain zero. In the demonstrated example, isolated color-2 noise outside the panels stayed unchanged, while each in-panel marker produced a 3×3 patch of 1s with the center 2.",

name: arc-panel-marker-expansion
description: Use when ARC grids show 2 markers near solid 3 panels; expand them into 1 patches.
---

# Expand markers around color-3 panels

In the demonstrated task, the grid has one or more rectangular color-3 panels, with scattered color-2 markers. Each relevant color-2 marker is the center of a 3×3 patch of color 1, while the original center remains color 2. Preserve all unaffected cells and grid dimensions.

## Procedure

1. Locate the large rectangular regions/panels of color 3.
2. Identify color-2 markers associated with those panels. Markers embedded in panels are relevant. Markers just outside a panel may also be relevant when their 3×3 patch touches the panel; use examples to determine which are intended.
3. For each relevant marker, set every in-bounds cell within one row and one column of its center to 1, except leave the center itself 2. This patch may extend beyond the panel into nearby background cells.
4. Preserve all other 0s, 2s, and 3s; overlapping patches combine while retaining any 2 centers.
5. Keep the original dimensions.

## Pitfalls

- Do not fill entire panels or change all 3s.
- Do not change isolated 2 markers far from panels.
- Check panel-border markers carefully: their 3×3 patch can extend into the surrounding 0 background.
- Generate output mechanically from the input grid, then check dimensions and that every original 2 is preserved.",
